title: kate-core: newline uses the indenter name
summary: newline_cmd calls newline_for_indenter with the syntax indenter name. A python colon then adds four spaces. CStyle matches in either case. The test goes in the existing workspace tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: workspace.rs has 3363 lines. Edit only newline_cmd and replace uses_cstyle. The file has one test module. It is mod tests inside workspace.rs. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Do not reformat the rest of the file. Delete uses_cstyle. Add indenter_name. It reads doc.syntax.definition. When that id is absent it returns None. Otherwise it returns ws.syntax.definition(id).indenter.clone(). In newline_cmd, replace the cstyle flag and the newline_insertion call. Call indenter_name before the fan_out block. Inside the closure call indent::newline_for_indenter(indenter.as_deref(), buffer, selection.min(), &config). Leave the rest of newline_cmd unchanged. The existing test cstyle_definition_adds_one_unit_on_newline stays green. Add python_definition_indents_after_a_colon in that same mod tests. Copy the language XML from that existing test. One copy uses name Py, extensions *.py, and indenter python. One copy uses name CStyleLang, extensions *.csx, and indenter CStyle. Use the existing newline_on helper. Py on def f(): returns def f(): plus a newline plus four spaces. Py on def f() returns def f() plus a newline. No syntax on def f(): returns def f(): plus a newline. CStyleLang on four spaces, foo, and a brace returns that line, a newline, and eight spaces. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: workspace::tests::python_definition_indents_after_a_colon
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. Enter after def f(): with indenter python inserts only a newline. After the change it inserts a newline and four spaces. Enter after def f() inserts only a newline. A missing syntax on def f(): inserts only a newline. Enter after four spaces, foo, and a brace with indenter CStyle inserts a newline and eight spaces.
